If you thrive in a dynamic hotel/tourism environment, take pride in supporting the financial function, and want to live and work in one of Australia's most iconic natural settings - this could be the role for you.   Benefits   Competitive Salary Package $68,000 - $78,000   Full time and ongoing position  Work in one of Australia’s most iconic tourism destinations  Career development and progression opportunities  Employee discounts on tours and accommodation worldwide  Supportive and inclusive team culture       Task & responsibilities  C   Qualification & experience   Relevant tertiary qualification in Finance, Business or related discipline  2 years' previous experience as an Accounts Clerk or related position  Sound knowledge and understanding of financial and accounting procedures, policies and systems  Advanced computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite and financial software   About Company    Nestled in the heart of Kakadu National Park, Cooinda Lodge Kakadu is more than just a destination—it’s an experience. Surrounded by breathtaking landscapes, ancient Indigenous culture, and rich biodiversity, our lodge serves as a gateway to one of Australia's most iconic and sacred places.   Our Mission   At Cooinda Lodge Kakadu, our mission is to deliver exceptional hospitality experiences that connect guests with the beauty, culture, and spirit of Kakadu National Park. We strive to create unforgettable moments, ensuring every visitor leaves with a deep appreciation for this unique landscape and its people.   Our Values   We are guided by a commitment to:   Authenticity – Honouring the rich cultural heritage of the land and its Traditional Owners.  Excellence – Delivering high-quality service and unforgettable experiences.  Sustainability – Protecting our environment and promoting responsible tourism.  Inclusivity – Fostering a diverse, welcoming workplace where everyone is valued.  Community Engagement – Supporting and collaborating with Indigenous communities.    An Inclusive and Supportive Work Culture   At Cooinda Lodge Kakadu, we celebrate diversity and strive to create a workplace where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered. Our team is made up of individuals from different backgrounds and cultures, all united by a shared passion for hospitality, nature, and Indigenous heritage.  We are committed to:   Equal opportunities for career growth and development.  Cultural appreciation and learning, including working closely with the local Indigenous community.   A supportive and team-oriented environment, where collaboration and respect are at the core of everything we do.    Our Achievements   Cooinda Lodge Kakadu is proud of its continued recognition as a premier eco-tourism destination. Some of our key accomplishments include:   Award-winning Indigenous tourism experiences, such as our Yellow Water Cruises, led by local guides sharing their deep knowledge of the land and its stories.  Sustainable tourism initiatives, including water conservation, energy-efficient operations, and eco-friendly accommodation practices.  Strong partnerships with Indigenous communities, ensuring authentic cultural representation and meaningful employment opportunities.  Consistently high guest satisfaction for our exceptional service, accommodation, and unique cultural experiences.    Join Our Team   When you work at Cooinda Lodge Kakadu, you become part of something special—a team dedicated to delivering inspiring experiences, protecting the environment, and celebrating Indigenous culture. Whether you're serving guests, guiding tours, or supporting lodge operations, your role contributes to a truly meaningful mission. MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Enrolled Nurse (504177)





 Department of Health

 Hospitals & Primary Care - Hospitals Nth

 Launceston General Hospital





 Applications must be submitted by Sunday 12 July, 2026 11:55 PM 




Position details




 

 

 
Applications close:

 
Sunday 12 July, 2026 11:55 PM AEST

 

 

 
Award-Classification:

 
Nurses and Midwives (Tasmanian State Service) Award, Enrolled Nurse, Grade 2

 

 

Salary:

$73,109 to $80,524 per annum


 
 

 
Employment type:

 
Permanent, part-time

 

 

 
Region:

 
North

 

 

Located in:

LGH Charles Street, Launceston


 

 
Job description:

 
Join our team and make a real difference every day! As an Enrolled Nurse, you'll play a vital role in delivering compassionate, patient-centred care to those who need it most. Working closely under the guidance of a Registered Nurse or Midwife, you'll provide hands-on support to patients and clients, ensuring their individual needs are met and their care plans are achieved.
This is your opportunity to grow your skills, work collaboratively in a supportive clinical environment, and contribute to positive health outcomes-while making meaningful connections with the people you care for.

 

 






 

The Team

Ward 6D is a 32-bed medical and stroke unit where the team provides quality and safe care and work within the CARE values of the organisation. 

Our leadership team consists of the Nurse Unit Manager, Clinical Nurse Educator, Associate Nurse unit Manager. The ANUM does not have a patient load allowing them to efficiently manage each shift. A clinical support nurse supports the team on early shifts and assists with access and flow. 

We pride ourselves on being a supportive, dedicated, respectful, and kind team where quality and safety is at the centre of our patient care.

The Role

Assess, plan, implement, and evaluate nursing care for patients with acute medical and stroke-related conditions.

Monitor and manage patients' vital signs, neurological status, and overall health.

Administer medications, treatments, and therapies safely and in accordance with clinical guidelines.

Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary teams including doctors, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and speech therapists.

Provide education and emotional support to patients and their families.

Maintain accurate and timely patient records, including care plans and observation charts.

Respond promptly to emergencies and deteriorations, initiating appropriate interventions.

Contribute to ongoing professional development and training within the team.

You will need 

A solid understanding of acute medical conditions and stroke care management.

Strong collaboration with all members of the multidisciplinary team to deliver holistic care.

Strong clinical assessment skills to accurately monitor patient conditions and identify signs of deterioration in an acute care setting

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Why Tasmania

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania's public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

Details of appointment

Permanent part time, shift worker (fully rotational) position, working 48 hours per fortnight, commencing 31 August 2026.

*notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary

$73,109 to $80,524 per annum (Pro rata). Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary range is in accordance with Nurses and Midwives (Tasmania State Service) Agreement 2023.

In addition, the following allowances calculated on the salaried incremental point may be available: 

Post Graduate Allowance of up to 7.5% based on qualification type

Salary Packaging 

You'll have access to salary package a range of benefits including living expenses up to $9,010 + $2,650 in meal entertainment each FBT year + other benefits if eligible. 

Benefits available to eligible candidates 

Professional development and accelerated pathways.

A range of leave entitlements, including study leave and Professional Development Support.

Fitness Passport - You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $14.50 per week per person, or $28.05 for a family.

Department of Health has achieved the "Carer Accredited Employer Status" providing support to employees with caring responsibilities. (Find out more under the Carer Recognition Act 2023). 

More information about our Employee Benefits can be found here

Eligibility

Successful applicants will be required to meet the essential criteria.

Registered with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia as an Enrolled Nurse (holds a Board-approved qualification in administration of medicines)

Note: - Please refer to the Application Guide for more information of pre-employment check.

Download the Statement of Duties and any Associated Documents

We encourage you to review the Statement of Duties, Applicant Guide, prior to applying for an overview of the duties, program, selection process and application guidance.

How to apply:

Apply Online. Please click the "Apply" button on this screen to ensure that important questions about you are answered.

You will be prompted to complete a 1-2 page application detailing your experience, skills and knowledge as they relate to the attached Statement of Duties. A separate statement addressing the selection criteria in the Statement of Duties is not required.

*applications from Recruitment Agencies will not be accepted for this role

Job title:  Speech Pathologist 

  Job type:  Contractor, flexible (2 - 4 days/week) 

  Work setting:  In-clinic and home visits 

  Salary offer:  40% on billings or $90 - $100 (depending on experience) 

  Location:  Mount Pritchard and communities within local LGA 

   

  About the company:  

 Our client is a well-established allied health provider committed to delivering tailored, innovative, and evidence-based therapy services to children, adolescents, and adults with diverse support needs. Their multidisciplinary team is passionate about helping individuals improve their quality of life and achieve meaningful outcomes through personalised therapy interventions. 

 With a strong focus on inclusion, diversity, and early intervention, they support individuals with a wide range of developmental, communication, and physical challenges. Their experienced clinicians work collaboratively with families, carers, and support networks to ensure every client receives the highest standard of care. 

 The practice has a special interest in early intervention and extensive experience supporting clients with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), ADHD, Intellectual Disability, Cerebral Palsy, Down Syndrome, Global Developmental Delay, Language Disorders, and Speech Disorders. 

   

  About the role:  

 An exciting opportunity is available for an experienced Speech Pathologist to join a supportive and growing multidisciplinary team on a contractor basis. 

 This role is primarily clinic-based, with occasional community visits within the local area and limited telehealth services when required. Community appointments are generally located within a short distance of the clinic. 

 The successful clinician will work with a varied caseload, predominantly paediatric clients, while also having opportunities to support adolescents and adults depending on their interests and experience. 

 Key responsibilites: 

 
	 Conduct comprehensive speech pathology assessments and interventions 
	 Develop individualised, evidence-based therapy plans 
	 Provide support for children, adolescents, and adults with communication and developmental needs 
	 Collaborate with families, carers, educators, and other healthcare professionals 
	 Complete clinical documentation and reports in a timely manner 
	 Participate in team discussions, supervision, and professional development activities 
 

   

  Benefits:  

 
	 Attractive contractor arrangement with a typical 60/40 fee split (dependent on experience) 
	 Option for 2–4 days per week, with preference for 3–4 days 
	 Long-term opportunity with an established client base 
	 Full administrative support, including dedicated administration staff and practice management 
	 Ongoing mentorship and supervision from experienced clinicians 
	 Collaborative multidisciplinary team environment 
	 Travel reimbursement at $0.99 per kilometre for community visits 
	 Established systems and processes to support clinical success 
	 Flexibility to provide telehealth services when appropriate 
	 July or August commencement available 
   Apply Now
